name: What should I do if construction costs start going over budget?

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my single-family home construction project starts going over budget?
mainEntity.text: What should I do if my single-family home construction project starts going over budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a project starts going over budget, the first step is to slow down decisions and identify the source of the overage. Often the issue is not one big problem but a combination of allowance shortfalls, change orders, site conditions, and upgrades made during construction. Ask for an updated cost-to-complete report so the remaining budget is clear. Then separate true overruns from optional upgrades. In some cases, the solution is to simplify finishes, adjust selections, or delay nonessential items like landscaping or specialty features. In other cases, the original estimate may have missed site work or key allowances and needs to be corrected. The important thing is to address the issue early, before the budget gap gets larger. Owners should also review whether future changes are being priced properly so the problem does not repeat. A transparent builder should explain the reasons for the overage and present practical options.
acceptedAnswer.description: If costs are rising, stop approving changes, review allowances and exclusions, and ask for a detailed cost-to-complete update. The best response is to identify which items are driving the overage and decide whether to reduce scope, change finishes, or add contingency.
